As of 400 AM EDT Friday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Scattered showers and storms are expected today and 
Saturday. Some storms may be severe with damaging wind gusts and 
isolated large hail possible.

Aloft, the ridge remains in place today from the Great Lakes into 
the Southeast with a trough across SE Canada into New England. The 
trough slides farther south today while the ridge become more 
amplified into the Northern Plains. As such, the belt of NW flow 
aloft shifts a bit south over the local area. This will place the 
entire local area under the favorable corridor for storms which 
stretches from the southern Great Lakes and Ohio SE into VA. Will 
note that clusters of storms have already formed across Wisconsin (E 
and NW). These storm complexes may continue to follow the NW flow 
and approach the local area later this afternoon into this evening. 
As is typical in NW flow MCS patterns, CAMs may not have a good 
handle on how long this convection persists and especially 
whether or not it can survive crossing the mountains. As such, 
will need to monitor the mesoscale environment as well as 
satellite and radar trends through the day to get a better idea
as to whether or not the convection looks like it can make it 
here.

With falling upper heights and the approaching front, scattered to 
potentially numerous storms are expected to develop during the 
afternoon and spread southeast through the evening. Given the 
overall favorable severe parameters of adequate CAPE and 0-6km shear 
of 30-45 kt, any storms that do form have the potential to become 
severe with damaging winds and isolated large hail the primary 
hazards. DCAPE will likely also be high, further supporting the 
damaging wind potential. The lack of low level shear and generally 
high LCLs will likely limit any tornado threat. Given the
favorable synoptic setup, SPC has maintained the Slight Risk 
(Level 2 out of 5) for severe weather across the entire area 
today. Convection should taper off this evening, however, SPC 
does note the potential for an overnight round of convection 
moving into WV which may need to be watched in case it can make 
it across the mountains.

By Sat, the trough builds closer to the local area, pushing a cold 
front slowly through. However, recent trends have been for a slower 
FROPA with the front potentially stalling just south of the FA.
As it stands, the current forecast maintains N/NNW winds Sat 
afternoon which is generally unfavorable for severe weather. 
Nevertheless, a sufficient overlap of CAPE and shear will likely
remain across the FA with higher instability across southern 
portions of the area. As such, forcing from another shortwave 
embedded within the NW flow aloft should be enough for at least 
scattered showers and storms Sat afternoon into Sat evening with
the best chance across the SW/S portions of the area. SPC has a
Marginal risk for severe storms Sat generally along and south 
of I-64 with a Slight risk across NE NC and extreme S VA. The 
main threat will once again be damaging winds, although, 
isolated large hail is also possible if more discrete 
convection/supercells are able to form.

Severe weather will not be the only potential hazard. WPC has placed 
the entire FA under a Marginal Risk for Excessive Rainfall (ERO) 
today with most of the area (apart from portions of the Northern 
Neck and Eastern Shore) under a Marginal Risk again on Sat. In fact, 
WPC has even placed a small Slight ERO across extreme SE VA and NE 
NC Sat (including portions of the Hampton Roads) given the potential 
for heavy rain and localized flooding. Fortunately, given the shear 
in place, individual showers/storms should be moving both days which 
should help limit the flooding potential outside of training. 
Shower/storm chances decrease Sun (15-40% PoPs) to mainly the SW 
half of the FA. Beyond Sun, dry conditions are expected for early 
next week.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Hot and humid conditions continue today with Heat 
Advisories in effect for portions of central and SE VA as well as NE 
NC along and east of I-95.

With the ridge remaining in place today and the cold front well to 
the north, another hot and humid day is expected. Highs this 
afternoon will likely reach the upper 90s SW with potentially only 
lower 90s NE. Meanwhile, dew points likely remain generally in the 
low-mid 70s apart from the SW Piedmont where mixing may allow for 
locally upper 60s dew points. This will allow for yet another day 
with heat indices at or above 100F for most of the area. The hottest 
conditions look to be across portions of central VA and SE VA into 
NE NC where heat indices of 105-109F are possible. As such, have 
kept Heat Advisories in place for these areas. Farther to the north 
into the Northern Neck, confidence is lower in reaching above 105F
